title: Interfacial Electron Injection and Charge-Carrier Suppression in Graphene Quantum Dot-Modified TiO₂ for Photocatalytic Mineralization of Textile Azo Dyes
content: The development of efficient visible-light-responsive photocatalysts for the mineralization of persistent azo dyes in textile effluents remains a critical environmental challenge. In this study, a hybrid nanocomposite consisting of MIL-125(Ti)-derived TiO2 coupled with graphene quantum dots (GQDs) was synthesized via a controlled solvothermal calcination route and evaluated for the photocatalytic degradation of Reactive Black 5 under visible-light irradiation (λ = 420–700 nm, intensity = 100 mW cm−2). The MIL-125(Ti) precursor was synthesized at 150 °C for 24 h and subsequently calcined at 450 °C for 3 h in air to obtain anatase-phase TiO2 with a crystallite size of 18.6 nm. GQDs with an average diameter of 4.2 ± 0.4 nm (n = 100) were incorporated at a loading of 3.0 wt% through ultrasonic-assisted self-assembly. The resulting composite exhibited a bandgap reduction from 3.21 eV for pure TiO2 to 2.64 eV, enabling efficient visible-light absorption. Photocatalytic studies revealed a dye decolorization efficiency of 97.8% within 120 min and total organic carbon (TOC) removal of 91.3% (± 1.8%, reducing TOC from an initial equilibrium concentration of 13.56 mg L−1 to 1.18 mg L−1) after 180 min. The enhanced performance was attributed to bandgap narrowing, visible-light sensitization, and interfacial electron transfer between GQDs and TiO2 that suppressed electron–hole recombination. The reaction followed pseudo-first-order kinetics with an apparent rate constant of 0.031 ± 0.002 min−1 (R2 = 0.985). Radical scavenging experiments confirmed the concurrent participation of superoxide radicals (O2•−), photogenerated holes (h+), and hydroxyl radicals (•OH). The hybrid catalyst demonstrated excellent stability with a degradation efficiency retention of 94.6% after five cycles.
